questionReadAloudEn:
What is the engineering design
process?
answerReadAloudEn:
The engineering design process is
the set of steps engineers follow
when creating solutions to solve a
problem
questionReadAloudEs:
En qué consiste el proceso de
 diseño de ingeniería?
answerReadAloudEs:
El proceso de diseño de ingeniería
 son los pasos que siguen los
 ingenieros cuando crean
 soluciones para resolver un
 problema

questionReadAloudEn:
When developing possible solutions to a
problem, engineers need to consider the
criteria and constraints of their design
solution.
What are criteria and constraints?
answerReadAloudEn:
Criteria = The requirements that
make it a good solution
Constraints = The limitations you
are allowed to work with
questionReadAloudEs:
A la hora de desarrollar posibles
soluciones a un problema, los
ingenieros deben tener en cuenta
los criterios y las limitaciones de su
solución de diseño.
¿Qué son los criterios y las
restricciones?
answerReadAloudEs:
Criterios = Los requisitos que la
hacen una buena solución
Restricciones = Las limitaciones
con las que puedes trabajar

questionReadAloudEn:
Describe the following steps of the
Engineering Design Process:
 ●​Research
 ●​Design
 ●​Prototype
 d)
answerReadAloudEn:
●​ Research - gather
 information to develop ideas.
 ●​ Design - take the ideas from
 research and make a drawing.
 ●​ Prototype - take the drawing
 and make a physical model
 )
questionReadAloudEs:
Describa las siguientes etapas del
 proceso de diseño técnico:
 - Investigación
 - Diseño
 - Prototipo
 )
answerReadAloudEs:
●​Investigación: recopilar
 información para desarrollar
 ideas.
 ●​Diseño: tomar las ideas de la
 investigación y hacer un
 dibujo.
 ●​Prototipo: a partir del dibujo,
 crear un modelo físico.

questionReadAloudEn:
When engineers are deciding which
materials to use in their prototypes, they
must consider the material’s properties.
List at least 3 examples of
properties engineers may
consider. (*Try all 5!*)
answerReadAloudEn:
●​ Flexibility
 ●​ Transparency (see through)
 ●​ Waterproof
 ●​ Thermal Conductor or
 Insulator
 ●​ Electrical Conductor or
 Insulator
questionReadAloudEs:
Cuando los ingenieros deciden qué
materiales utilizar en sus
prototipos, deben tener en cuenta
sus propiedades.
Enumera al menos 3 ejemplos de
propiedades que los ingenieros
pueden tener en cuenta. (*Bono:
Consigue las 5*)
answerReadAloudEs:
●​ Flexibilidad
 ●​ Transparencia (transparente)
 ●​ Impermeabilidad
 ●​ Conductor o aislante térmico
 ●​ Conductor o aislante eléctrico

questionReadAloudEn:
Draw AND explain Earth’s place in
the Universe.
answerReadAloudEn:
Our Earth is in the Solar System, which is
 in the Milky Way Galaxy, which is in the
 Universe.

questionReadAloudEn:
What is gravity?
 )

1.​Describe how mass
 impacts an object’s gravity.
 2.​Describe how distance
 impact an object’s gravity.
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​An object with more mass will
 have stronger gravity.
 a.​
 2.​The closer (less distance) two
 objects are, the stronger the
 gravity.

questionReadAloudEn:
What causes the moon to look
different every night?
answerReadAloudEn:
As the Moon moves around the
Earth, sunlight hits different parts
of the Moon - which is the part
that we see.

The Moon moves between Sun and
Earth, and blocks the Sun’s light
from hitting Earth.
 )

questionReadAloudEn:
Draw AND Describe what happens
during a lunar eclipse
answerReadAloudEn:
The Earth moves between the Sun
and the Moon and blocks most of
the Sun’s light from hitting the
Moon.

questionReadAloudEn:
1.​What is the continental drift
 theory?
 2.​Name at least one piece of
 evidence that supports this
 theory.
 b)
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​The idea that the continents were
 once joined together and have
 moved apart over time.
 2.​
 The continents look like they
 would fit together like a puzzle.
 OR
 Fossils of the same organisms
 have been found on different
 continents.
 b)

questionReadAloudEn:
What does the Law of Superposition
tell us about the ages of the rock
layers and fossils in those rock layers?
answerReadAloudEn:
The Law of Superposition explains the
oldest rock layers and fossils are on the
bottom and the younger rock layers and
fossils are on the top.

questionReadAloudEn:
1.​What is a fossil?
 2.​What can fossils tell us about
 Earth’s past?
 )
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​Fossils are remains or traces of
 plants and animals that
 existed long ago.
 2.​They provide evidence to show
 how Earth and organisms
 have changed over time.
 )

questionReadAloudEn:
Scientists often look for similarities in body parts
of fossils and modern animals.
What are the two major things that
these similarities can tell us?
answerReadAloudEn:
If animals have similar body parts, it
can mean:
 1.​They share a
 common
 ancestor in the
 past
 or
 2.​ They adapted
 in similar ways
 to live in the
 same kind of
 environment.

questionReadAloudEn:
What are the 5 things ALL
organisms need to be considered a
living thing?
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​Made of cells
 2.​ Uses energy
 3.​Responds to surroundings
 4.​Grows and develops
 5.​Reproduces

questionReadAloudEn:
1.​Describe a unicellular
 organism.
 2.​Describe a multicellular
 organism.
answerReadAloudEn:
1. Unicellular organism - has just
ONE cell that performs all life
functions.
2. Multicellular organism - has
many specialized cells that perform
specific functions

questionReadAloudEn:
Cells have different parts called
organelles that allow them to carry out
functions of life.
Describe the function of the
following organelles:
 1.​Nucleus
 2.​Cell Membrane
 3.​Mitochondria
 4.​Vacuoles
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​Nucleus: Controls the cell
 2.​Cell Membrane: A barrier that
 protects the cell by controlling
 what comes in and out of the
 cell
 3.​Mitochondria: Changes food
 into energy
 4.​Vacuoles: Stores important
 materials for the cell

questionReadAloudEn:
Plant cells have ALL the same organelles as
animal cells but also need 3 additional
organelles in order to help plants function
and live.
Describe the function of these 3
additional organelles that plant cells
have
 1.​Cell Wall
 2.​One Large Vacuole
 3.​Chloroplasts
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​Cell Wall: Provides structure
 and support
 2.​One Large Vacuole: Stores
 water
 a.​
 3.​ Chloroplasts: traps sun energy
 to create sugar (food) for the
 cell

questionReadAloudEn:
Below are examples of different parts of
Our bodies.
From top to bottom, name the part AND
describe how they fit together.
5b)

1.​ Describe the function of the skeletal
 system.
 2.​ Describe the function of the muscular
 system.
 3.​ Explain how they work together to
 make your body move.
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​ Skeletal System: Protects and
 supports your body
 2.​ Muscular System: Allows your body
 and organs to move
 3.​ Your muscles from your muscular
 system pull on your bones from your
 skeletal system to make your body
 move

questionReadAloudEn:
1.​Describe the function of the
 circulatory system
 2.​Describe the function of the
 respiratory system.
 3.​Explain how the circulatory
 system and respiratory system
 work together to move oxygen
 through your body.
 )
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​Circulatory System: Moves
 important things through your
 body using blood
 2.​Respiratory System: Allows you
 to breathe in oxygen and breathe
 out carbon dioxide
 3.​Your respiratory system brings
 oxygen into your body and your
 circulatory system moves it
 through your body.
 )

questionReadAloudEn:
Describe the function of the immune
system.
answerReadAloudEn:
The immune system defends your body
from disease

questionReadAloudEn:
Describe the function of the excretory
system.
answerReadAloudEn:
The excretory system filters toxic waste
and gets rid of it.

questionReadAloudEn:
1.​What is density?
 2.​How can we
 determine the
 relative density of
 different materials?
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​Density is how many
 particles are packed into
 a certain space.
 2.​Materials that are less
 dense will float on top
 of materials that are
 more dense.

questionReadAloudEn:
How do we calculate the
density of an object?
answerReadAloudEn: Density = Mass ÷ Volume

questionReadAloudEn:
1.​What is a pure
 substance?
 2.​Give one example of a
 pure substance.
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​A substance that cannot
 be separated into
 simpler parts.
 2.​Examples:
 ○​ Gold (Au)
 ○​ Oxygen (O)
 ○​ Salt (NaCl)
 ○​ Water (H20)

questionReadAloudEn:
1.​What is a mixture?
 2.​Give one example
 of a mixture.
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​A mixture is 2 or more
 substances combined
 that can be separated.
 2.​Examples of Mixtures:
 ○​ Salt Water (H20 + NaCl)
 ○​ Air
 ○​ Milk

questionReadAloudEn:
What does a wave do?
 b)
answerReadAloudEn:
A wave transfers energy
from one place to another
 b)

questionReadAloudEn:
1.​What are
 electromagnetic waves?
 2.​Give at least 3 examples
 of electromagnetic
 waves.
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​ Electromagnetic waves are invisible
 energy waves that travel through
 empty space on our planet and
 outer space.
 2.​ Examples:
 ●​ light waves
 ●​ radio waves
 ●​ microwaves
 ●​ ultraviolet waves
 ●​ x-rays
 ●​ gamma rays

questionReadAloudEn:
1.​What are mechanical
 waves?
 2.​Give an example of a
 mechanical wave.
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​Mechanical are waves that
 transfer energy through a
 substance
 2.​Examples:
 ○​ Sound waves
 ○​ Water waves

questionReadAloudEn:
Amplitude, wavelength, crest, and
trough are wave features.
Label each of these on the wave
diagram below
 )

Amplitude , frequency and
wavelength are wave features that
describe the energy traveling through
the wave.
Define these 3 wave
properties.
 f)
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​ Amplitude measures the strength of
 the wave’s energy.
 2.​ Frequency is the speed of the wave
 3.​ Wavelength measures the distance
 between waves
 f)

questionReadAloudEn:
​
What happens when a wave is
absorbed?
 h)
answerReadAloudEn:
When a wave is absorbed, its energy gets
taken in by the material it hits.
 h)

questionReadAloudEn:
What happens when a wave is
transmitted?
answerReadAloudEn:
When a wave is transmitted; the wave
passes through a substance (medium) and
continues to travel
